jobs.title: Environmental Program Manager
jobs.description:
Requisition Summary

The Environmental Program Manager leads and coordinates PACCAR Technical Center's environmental programs, management systems, compliance initiatives, sustainability objectives, and improvement portfolio. The role is the central point of coordination among Operations, Facilities, Engineering, Safety, Security, Corporate Environmental Affairs, regulatory agencies, consultants, contractors, and service providers.

This position provides program governance and strategic direction to ensure environmental commitments are planned, executed, monitored, and reported in alignment with federal, state, local, corporate, and ISO 14001 requirements. The Environmental Program Manager combines environmental subject-matter leadership with cross-functional program execution, audit readiness, risk management, performance tracking, and continuous improvement.

Company Information

PACCAR is a Fortune 500 company established in 1905 and recognized as a global leader in the commercial vehicle industry, with internationally recognized brands including Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF. PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture, and support of high-quality commercial vehicles, diesel engines, financial services, and information technology solutions.

The PACCAR Technical Center provides engineering excellence to PACCAR's truck and engine divisions through innovative product development and testing. Located in the Skagit Valley approximately 65 miles north of Seattle, the Technical Center supports PACCAR's global operations through advanced engineering and testing services.

Job Functions / Responsibilities

- Serve as the site leader for environmental programs, regulatory relationships, compliance risks, and strategic initiatives

- Develop program roadmaps, operating plans, priorities, milestones, metrics, and leadership reporting

- Lead cross-functional teams, align resources with business objectives, and prepare for emerging regulatory and operational requirements

- Administer and continuously improve the site ISO 14001 Environmental Management System (EMS), including policies, procedures, objectives, and documentation.

- Lead management reviews, internal and external audits, certification activities, performance reporting, and corrective actions.

- Manage environmental compliance, permits, inspections, audits, agency correspondence, corrective actions, and required reporting.

- Interpret requirements, maintain compliance calendars, and communicate obligations to leadership and operational teams.

- Represent the Technical Center during agency inspections, regulatory discussions, and corporate environmental reviews.

- Oversee hazardous and universal waste, wastewater, stormwater, SPCC, air quality and Title V, SARA/EPCRA, greenhouse gas reporting, hazardous materials, chemical management, Safety Data Sheets, and zero waste programs.

- Direct hazardous, industrial, and special waste characterization, storage, transportation, manifesting, and disposal.

- Integrate environmental compliance and sustainability requirements into operational planning and capital projects.

- Lead projects and initiatives that reduce environmental risk, emissions, waste, resource use, and operating costs while improving program maturity and audit outcomes.

- Apply Lean, Six Sigma, and project management principles to implement environmental best practices and support PACCAR stewardship goals.

- Manage consultants, auditors, contractors, waste service providers, scopes of work, schedules, deliverables, performance, contracts, and budgets.

- Build partnerships across site, corporate, regulatory, and external stakeholders to strengthen environmental awareness, accountability, and engagement.

- Develop and deliver environmental compliance training for employees, contractors, and new hires.

- Prepare reports, dashboards, presentations, executive updates, and employee communications.

- Provide technical guidance and mentoring to environmental staff and cross-functional teams, influencing results without direct authority.

Qualifications

- Experience with ISO 14001 or other management system frameworks, including audits and certification activities.

- 7+ years of experience leading environmental programs, projects, operations, compliance initiatives, or management systems.

- Demonstrated experience coordinating cross-functional teams and complex initiatives.

- Strong organizational, regulatory interpretation, problem-solving, written, verbal, and presentation skills.

- Ability to build relationships with regulators, corporate leadership, operational teams, consultants, and service providers.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and environmental data management systems.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Management , Environmental Science, Business, Engineering, Program Management, Sustainability, Public Administration, or related fields .

PACCAR Benefits

As a U.S. PACCAR employee, you have a full range of benefit options including:

- 401k with up to a 5% company match

- Fully funded pension plan that provides monthly benefits after retirement

- Comprehensive paid time off – minimum of 10 paid vacation days (additional days are provided with additional seniority/years of service), 12 paid holidays, and sick time

- Tuition reimbursement for continued education

- Medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your family

- Flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health savings account (HSA)

- Paid short-and long-term disability programs

- Life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance

- EAP services including wellness plans, estate planning, financial counseling and more

Additional Job Board Information

PACCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veteran/Disability and E-Verify Employer. At PACCAR, we value talent and promote growth and development. We carefully consider numerous compensation factors including your education, training, or experience. The salary range for the Environmental Program Manager is $104,100 - $162,900 annually. Additionally, this role is eligible for the full range of benefit options listed above.

jobs.description:

PACCAR Engine Company in Columbus, Mississippi produces the best-in-class, state-of-the-art MX engines that power Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF trucks. PACCAR MX engines bring a new level of innovation through quality, exceptional reliability, and proven performance. In more than 50 years, PACCAR has delivered over one million engines globally, providing innovative solutions and an unwavering commitment to superior performance. Join our best-in-class team today through the following opportunity:

Requisition Summary

The Site Operations Manager on the evening shift is responsible for managing a safe work environment, establishing, monitoring, and improving performance to plant/department goals. The Site Operations Manager is expected to manage multiple metrics, prepare and present operating plans and implement and drive PACCAR Production System initiatives.

Job Functions / Responsibilities

- The Site Operations Manager reports to the Plant Manager and is responsible for directing Manufacturing, Maintenance, and Materials activities to provide a quality product that meets customer demand safely.

- The primary job function is developing & managing front-line managers in multiple departments while ensuring plant goals are met.

- Maintains a collaborative work environment with colleagues and serves as a coach and mentor in the personal and professional development of team members.

- Supports the training, motivation, and safety of High-Performance Work Teams members and representatives.

- Oversees the distribution of work assignments to team members/representatives in accordance with the production objectives.

- Responsible for setting and meeting production goals, including safety, quality, delivery reliability, scrap, labor efficiency, and housekeeping.

- In conjunction with Human Resources, ensure appropriate hiring, orientation, training, performance reviews, counseling and disciplinary actions of employees.

- Prepares meaningful reports/analyses for management.

- Leads process improvement efforts such as PACCAR Production System which includes lean leadership, 5S, effective root cause and corrective action for repetitive issues, quality improvement initiatives, auditing, waste reduction, and Kaizen events.

- Champion multiple Six Sigma projects

- Assist in the research, creation, and management of department budgets, major plant projects involving cost reduction and new product manufacturing setup and implementation.

- Control monthly costs per the plant budget.

- Ensure local compliance with PACCAR quality programs. Maintain quality standards per ISO and IATF requirements.

- Assist in devising, reviewing and implementing methods for improving productivity and machine uptime.

- Maintain effective communication between departments to ensure maximum cost-savings and efficient manufacturing operations.

- Must be able to think strategically and develop strategic plans to meet company and facility objectives.

- Ensure compliance with division/corporate policies and procedures.

- Assist in the development of strategic direction for PACCAR Engine Company.

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Materials Management or related field required.

- 10 plus years of supervisory experience.

- Working knowledge of assembly and machining operations, continuous improvement tools and methodologies, and teambuilding skills.

- Ability to coach and develop all levels of employees.

- Possesses problem-solving skills with the ability to function equally well as a team leader.

- Demonstrated leadership and strong interpersonal skills.

- Ability to operate and actively participate in a team-oriented environment.

- Ability to initiate, gain buy-in, and lead change through continuous process improvements.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Previous experience with PACCAR is desirable.

- Experience in the application of lean leadership principles.

- Working knowledge of PACCAR personnel procedures is desirable.

U.S. Salaried Benefits

PACCAR offers comprehensive benefits from the time of hire through retirement for vested employees and their families. As a U.S. Salaried PACCAR employee, you have a full range of benefit options including:

The Emissions Compliance department consists of approximately 46 professionals who work with environmental regulatory agencies to manage engine emissions and vehicle GHG compliance. Each year, we perform compliance and regulatory tests on more than 1,000 on-board diagnostics and prepare more than 15,000 pages of documentation per engine to ensure PACCAR’s engines comply with U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), California Air Resources Board (CARB), and Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) regulations.

Requisition Summary

Join the Emissions Compliance team to lead program management of production compliance activities to provide testing and reporting that demonstrated our products comply with critical emissions, diagnostics, and related requirements. A successful candidate will be highly self-directed, adaptable, an excellent problem-solver, and the ability to work with all levels of the organization.

- Manage large program budget encompassing multiple projects including developing annual and longer-term budgets in coordination with Operations management, project managers, and Accounting, and provide updated monthly forecasts.

- Support team members to set up, maintain, track, and close projects in the project tracking system. Facilitate internal production compliance project review meetings on a monthly cadence.

- Support compliance teams in facilitating test article accounting and disposition at the conclusion of testing.

- Track and approve purchase orders.

Qualifications

- Minimum of seven years professional experience including three years’ experience in a program or project manager role.

- Proficiency with project and portfolio tracking tools and MS Office applications, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams.

- Working knowledge of production compliance, regulatory processes, product development or other related activites.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Strong interpersonal skills.

- Effectively communicate to all levels of the organization.

- Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities.

Kenworth Truck Company

Kenworth Truck Company, founded in 1923, is the manufacturer of The World’s Best® heavy and medium duty trucks. With an excellent heritage of quality, innovation and technology, Kenworth has played an essential role in the development of trucks that are more fuel efficient, productive, and economical to operate. Today, Kenworth is leading transportation innovation with the introduction of battery-electric vehicles, exploration of fuel cell electric powertrains, and autonomous driving systems. Kenworth is committed to fostering an environment of diversity, equality and inclusivity in the workplace.

Job Summary

Support the U.S. and Canadian Kenworth dealer network by developing a pipeline of diesel and technical school graduates who have completed Kenworth Essentials training. This position works with technical schools, Kenworth dealers, and internal training stakeholders to increase student participation and completion, align school engagement with dealer workforce needs, and support recruitment of qualified entry-level service technicians into the Kenworth dealer network.

This position is remote and requires up to 50% travel. The qualified candidate may be located anywhere in the continental U.S. or Canada; however, a Midwest location is preferred.

Duties

- Identify and develop partnerships between Kenworth Truck Company, Kenworth dealers, and the Kenworth Dealer Service Training department to implement training programs that support the recruiting, training, and retention of prospective heavy-duty truck and diesel service technicians.

- Work with individual technical schools to increase student participation in and completion of the Kenworth Essentials program.

- Collaborate with sponsoring Kenworth dealers in local markets to support ongoing program development, including dealer personnel involvement, equipment provisions, recruiting events, career fairs, and other educational opportunities.

- Coordinate database management and training program access through the BCA training website.

- Use available student and course data to identify trends, establish goals, and recommend strategies to improve program outcomes.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree strongly preferred; equivalent professional experience may be substituted.

- 7+ years of technical school instruction, management, or related technical training experience required.

- Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) certifications desired.

- Demonstrated ability to grow and manage large, complex programs.

- Outstanding verbal and written communication skills, including experience delivering formal presentations.

- Excellent computer skills, including proficiency with Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

- Previous experience working with or coordinating technical school programs highly desired.

- Previous experience with PACCAR MX engines highly desired.

- Previous experience in dealership service or service management within the commercial truck industry preferred.

- Demonstrated knowledge of heavy-duty truck products and manufacturing processes desired.

- Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to develop trusting business relationships.

- Diesel engine certifications or automotive OEM service certifications are a plus.

Relocation is not available.

- Global Fortune 500 Company with a wide array of growth and development opportunities

- Work alongside experienced goal-oriented colleagues recognized as experts in their fields

- Support and/or design the commercial vehicles of the future with a focus on emerging technologies such as electric and autonomous trucks

jobs.description:
Company Information

PACCAR is a Fortune 500 company established in 1905. PACCAR Inc. is recognized as a global leader in the commercial vehicle, financial, and customer service fields with internationally recognized brands such as Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF trucks. PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture and customer support of premium light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates and also provides customized financial services, information technology and truck parts related to its principal business.
Whether you want to design the transportation technology of tomorrow, support the staff functions of a dynamic, international leader, or build our excellent products and services, you can develop the career you desire with PACCAR. Get started!

Requisition Summary

The Trade Program Manager (TPM) will manage the operational entry process requests, such as HTS/ADD/CVD, STL/ALUM/CU, FTA and IOR in addition to any other import activity required to file a complaint entry. This position also manages compliance programs by performing audits on broker entries and ensuring adherence to import and export customs regulations. In addition, this position supports the International Compliance Manager and the compliance department with any tasks or activities required such as post entry correction projects, protest filing, trade remedies, and duty drawback programs among other activities.

Job Functions /Responsibilities:

Classifications:

-

- Responsible for accurate classifications of heavy truck components, equipment, prototypes and related products.

- Ability to interpret technical drawings and legal rulings to assign proper classifications.

- Verify accuracy of 3rd party classifications and coordinate workflow.

- Update HTS database timely and accurately.

- Provide timely responses to internal and external customers.

Antidumping and Countervailing Duties:

- Monitor anti-dumping (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) cases, report on potential cases that may impact PACCAR, and maintain records of current products subject to AD/CVD.

- Research and advise brokers on AD/CVD applicability.

- Monitor termination of cases.

Internal Audits and Controls:

- Conduct internal audits to identify broker, supplier and division compliance issues and work to resolve any issues identified to ensure regulatory compliance through the PACCAR supply chain.

- Report, address, and document internal audit findings.

Other Responsibilities:

- Perform other compliance related duties and/or projects as required, including, but not limited to responding to customs inquiries, duty drawback filings, broker/vendor/government payment processing, developing internal compliance training, proper record keeping, and broker invoice processing.

Qualifications & Skills:

- 5+ years of work experiece

- Bachelor’s degree in business, Logistics or International-related field

- Customs broker license required

- Three years of experience in trade compliance desired

- Strong classification skills

- Working knowledge of US & CA Customs laws and regulations

- Detail-oriented, with ability to identify and resolve entry filing errors

- Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, with ability to accurately describe/simplify complex customs terms/programs

- Ability to meet deadlines and work with a sense of urgency
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills

- Strong Excel, Access, and data analysis skills

- 401k with up to a 5% company match

- Fully funded pension plan that provides monthly benefits after retirement
